name: MarineCadastre Nationwide AIS 2023-2024 (daily files)
steward: NOAA Office for Coastal Management and BOEM
coverage_alaska: no (filtered out at the request of the Alaska Marine Data Exchange; probe found 1-3 stray ships per day)
coverage_hawaii: yes (16-27 large ships per sampled day)
fields: MMSI; IMO; type; length; SOG; time
notes: Puerto Rico and USVI also present (56-63 large ships per day); Guam present (12-16 per day)

name: MarineCadastre daily files 2015-2017
notes: IMO numbers are blank so the IMO rule can't be applied; a length-and-type-only filter is needed and must be validated in the lower 48 first; vessel types use codes 1001-1025 (for example 1004 freight; 1024 tank; 1012 passenger) that need the MarineCadastre crosswalk

name: MarineCadastre zone files 2009-2014 (file geodatabases)
coverage_alaska: yes (UTM zones 1-10; zone 6 July 2014 has 4.1 million reports and 332 vessels)
measure: point reports (Broadcast) plus Vessel and Voyage tables
fields: MMSI; type; length; IMO and name blank
notes: Monthly zone files of 2-133 MB each; needs pyogrio (OpenFileGDB) to read

name: NOAA AIS Vessel Transit Counts 2024
measure: transits per 100 m cell (all vessel groups)
notes: Independent processing of the same raw data; checks our pipeline not the raw data

name: World Bank Global Shipping Traffic Density
decision: candidate for Alaska and an independent check
notes: Different raw source from MarineCadastre; layers for commercial; passenger; oil and gas; fishing; leisure

name: North Pacific and Arctic Marine Vessel Traffic Dataset 2015-2020 (Kapsar and others 2022)
steward: NSF Arctic Data Center (authors at Ocean Conservancy and others)
access: public (article CC BY 4.0; dataset license to confirm)
coverage_alaska: yes (51-72 N; 162 E to 145 W; Bering; Aleutians; Cook Inlet; Prince William Sound)
measure: unique ships (MMSI) per hexagon; distance traveled per raster cell
fields: none (identity removed); types cargo; tanker; fishing; other
resolution: 625 km2 hexagons; 10 and 25 km rasters; 1 km within 10 km of shore
license: to confirm on the Arctic Data Center record
notes: Counts unique ships like our method but has no 100 m length filter; cargo plus tanker is the closest match; hexagons too coarse for routes but good for validation and offshore lanes

name: AIS Vessel Traffic Data - Alaska - USCG Terrestrial - Monthly Totals (Axiom)
notes: Possible cross-check for the 2009-2016 MarineCadastre Alaska records

name: Arctic Oil Spill Risk Assessment vessel density (Axiom)
steward: Axiom Data Science (from Marine Exchange of Alaska AIS)

name: PacIOOS AIS Ship Traffic Hawaii 2008-2009 and 2011-2012
measure: binned counts (1 km) and point data
notes: Older but independent of MarineCadastre processing

name: Global Fishing Watch AIS vessel presence
access: public API (free registration; terms to confirm)
measure: hours of presence (one position per vessel per hour)
fields: filter by vessel type and flag
notes: Current years with satellite coverage; needs an API token; confirm the license allows use in a government report

name: Arctic Ship Traffic Data (ASTD)
access: government only (Level I free for signatory national agencies including the United States)
measure: ship-level AIS with identity at Level I
notes: Not public; would match our method for Arctic Alaska

name: USCG NAIS historical data by agency request
notes: Would match our method exactly for 2023-2024

name: USACE Principal Ports tonnage
decision: used (port list and a rank check)
notes: Rank check: Spearman 0.74 between ship counts and foreign tons for the 73 deep-draft ports
